sections.title: Local remediation, fitting in log space

keyTerms.definition: A power law mapping compute, params, or data to loss. The log transform turns the curve into a line.
Loss versus model size at fixed compute. It is U-shaped; the bottom is the optimal N/D split.
The N/D point at the bottom of the isoFLOP curve. In the symmetric toy, N and D each scale as C^0.5.
Writing the predicted number, band, and decision rule before the data arrives.
log(L_obs) minus log(L_pred). Random scatter means noise; a smile or frown means the functional form is wrong.
Training past the optimal token/param ratio. Each extra token buys less loss reduction.

recall.question: What is the 6ND budget rule, and what are its two knobs?
recall.answer: Six FLOPs per parameter per token: two for forward, four for backward. Multiply by tokens. N and D are the two knobs.

recall.question: Why is inference-optimal different from compute-optimal?
recall.answer: Compute-optimal minimizes loss at fixed training FLOPs. Inference-optimal adds deployment cost over the serving lifetime, favoring smaller models trained longer.

recall.question: What three limits bound scale transfer?
recall.answer: The law can change form, the noise regime changes with fewer runs at scale, and the optimum can move outside the searched range.
